title: Map Tile Center Calculator: Middle of a Tile
description: Compute the centre coordinate of a map tile with the Map Tile Center Calculator — the lat/lon a z/x/y tile is centred on. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the centre of Times Square's z15 tile is not Times Square — it is the middle of a 926-metre square containing it, offset by wherever the point fell inside its tile.
quick_answer: The Map Tile Center Calculator computes the latitude/longitude at the centre of a z/x/y map tile. Enter the tile and read its middle point — for centring maps on tiles, labelling tile footprints, and understanding why a map centred 'on the tile' is not centred on your place.

A tile archive indexed by centre points becomes searchable geography instead of anonymous numbers.
“Why did the map centre miss the cafe?” — because it centred the tile. The centre calculator quantifies the miss: up to half a tile diagonal.
Tile centres form a ready-made systematic sample grid at any zoom — a sampling frame hiding in the map stack.
At z15 a tile spans ~926 m in New York, so its centre can sit up to ~650 m (half-diagonal) from any point inside. At z10 the same miss can reach ~27 km — the zoom chooses the error's scale.

body.t: The centre is computed in pixel space (the tile's middle pixel converted back) — its latitude is the Mercator middle, not the arithmetic mean of the edge latitudes. The distinction is small per tile and exactly the kind this family refuses to blur.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
The geographic coordinate of a tile's centre pixel — converting (x + 0.5, y + 0.5) in tile units back through the Mercator inverse.
Which map standard does it use?
The slippy-map standard (Web Mercator, 256-px tiles) shared by OSM, Google and MapLibre.
Can I use this in production GIS?
The formulas are the production standard itself — yes for web-mapping work.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — tile systems are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — tiles and pixels quantise; decimals beyond the cell are decoration.
Centre of the bounds instead?
Averaging edge latitudes is close but not identical (Mercator curvature within the tile). This calculator returns the pixel-space centre, the renderer's truth.
Can I centre a Leaflet/MapLibre map on it?
Yes — the pair is an ordinary centre coordinate for any map call.
Which tile contains a point?
The Lat Lon to Map Tile Calculator — centres and containment are sibling questions with different tools.
Centres as labels?
A centre label names the tile's middle ground — honest for cataloguing, misleading if read as a feature location. Label responsibly.
z/x/y of the centre's own tile?
Itself, by construction — the centre always falls in its own tile, a fixed point of the system worth noticing once.
